title: fix(app-shell): correct the flow `loop` node's Item-variable hint to the identifier the spec applies
body:
Fixes #9340

The flow `loop` group's "Item variable" box hinted `currentItem` while `LoopConfigSchema`
applies a different identifier to the omitted key. A `text` control's placeholder is drawn
muted and is never written, so what it states is precisely *the name you get if you leave
this blank* — and it named the wrong one. An author who read the hint and wrote that
reference in the loop body got an **unresolved reference at run time**.

## Which half of the fix this is

**The minimum honest fix**: `loop`'s placeholder now carries the identifier the spec applies.

⛔ **Not** the other half — holding the hint and the spec default together mechanically needs
the `text` / `number` controls to read `defaultValue`, which is objectui#9109's fence 4 and is
not built here.

⭐ And the fence in between, which the card calls the interesting part: **declaring a
`defaultValue` would not have fixed this.** The `defaultValue` doc comment on
`FlowConfigField` names exactly three read sites — `controllerAdmits`, the `boolean` control,
the `select` control — and a `text` control is none of them, so such a declaration is inert on
screen. The pin asserts the absence of one, paired with a lit control proving the slot is
reachable from this table, so the `undefined` is a deliberate non-declaration.

## How the `loop` descriptor was identified — structurally, never by line

The card cites `:512` / `:519`; the claim comment re-read them as `:595` / `:602`; they have
moved again since. The two rows are near-identical text, so neither a line number nor the
`placeholder` string can address one of them. Two independent structural anchors were used:

1. **A group-boundary sweep** over the `FLOW_NODE_CONFIG` object literal (the technique
   objectui#9335 used in this same file): walk the literal tracking bracket depth, record each
   top-level group key's body span, then report which span each `iteratorVariable` row falls
   in. It resolved the `loop` group's body and the `map` group's body as disjoint ranges and
   placed exactly one row in each. The edit script re-ran that sweep and **asserted** both that
   exactly one candidate row sat inside the `loop` span and that it did **not** sit inside the
   `map` span, before writing a byte.
2. **The runtime accessor** `fieldsForNodeType('loop')` — the same alias-aware entry point
   `FlowNodeInspector` itself calls, which hands back the owning group's own array. Every
   assertion in the pin goes through it; none addresses a line.

The resulting diff touches the `loop` group only — `map` has no hunk.

## The spec probe, re-derived at this head

⛔ The card's table was not taken. Run against the installed `@objectstack/spec` (17.4.0),
printing accepted rows beside refusals so a refusal is a reading rather than a dead probe, and
**pushing past the first accepted value** per objectui#9336:

```
installed @objectstack/spec = 17.4.0
ACCEPT  L1 minimum accepted body
        in : {"collection":"{leadList}"}
        out: {"collection":"{leadList}","iteratorVariable":"item"}
        -> iteratorVariable materialises as: "item"
ACCEPT  L4 explicit iteratorVariable = the FORM HINT
        in : {"collection":"{leadList}","iteratorVariable":"currentItem"}
        out: {"collection":"{leadList}","iteratorVariable":"currentItem"}
ACCEPT  L5 explicit iteratorVariable = the SPEC DEFAULT
        out: {"collection":"{leadList}","iteratorVariable":"item"}
REFUSE  L6 alias `itemVariable`
        !  unrecognized_keys: Unrecognized key(s) on this loop container config: `itemVariable`.
           Did you mean `itemVariable` -> `iteratorVariable`? ...
REFUSE  L7 bogus sibling key (strictObject control)
        !  unrecognized_keys: ... `currentItem` ...
REFUSE  L9 iteratorVariable empty string
        !  too_small: expected string to have >=1 characters

==================== MapConfigSchema (LIT CONTROL — the one that agrees) ====================
ACCEPT  M1 minimum accepted body
        out: {"collection":"{items}","flowName":"one_task_signoff","iteratorVariable":"item"}
ACCEPT  M4 explicit iteratorVariable = "currentItem"     <- accepted there too
REFUSE  M5 bogus sibling key (strictObject control)

==================== VERDICT ====================
loop applies : "item"
map  applies : "item"
```

**Two readings the card's table does not carry, both from pushing past the first accept:**

- ⭐ **The wrong hint was itself a VALID value.** `L4` is ACCEPTED and materialises verbatim.
  So this was never a value the contract refuses — it was a hint naming something the author
  had to *type* for it to be true, in a slot that means the opposite. That is exactly why the
  repair is a corrected hint and not a lenient parse, and why the pin also asserts that a
  **stored** `currentItem` still round-trips untouched (AGENTS.md #0.1 — no renderer-side
  rewriting of an author's explicit choice).
- The spec's declared `aliases: { itemVariable: 'iteratorVariable' }` does **not** make the
  alias acceptable (`L6` refuses); it only enriches the suggestion in the refusal message.
  Behaving as designed — recorded, not filed.

`L9` is the sibling constraint sitting behind the first accept: a value-level `min(1)` that
survives past the key-level strictness.

## Locale reach

`localizeFlowFields` overlays label / help / options / columns and **never** `placeholder`, so
the hint is locale-invariant and this one edit reaches the zh-CN author too. Pinned, with the
label as the lit control (the same call *does* change it), so a no-op overlay cannot be what
makes the hint survive.

## Test scope actually run

⚠️ The whole tree, not just the file I wrote — and no shard was used anywhere.

| run | result |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/` | **78 files, 929 passed, 1 skipped** |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (superset) | **261 files, 2751 passed, 1 skipped** |
| `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) | exit 0 |
| 17 targeted `check:*` gates | all exit 0 |

Both vitest runs and the gate re-run were repeated on the final rebased head, **800fc9c**.

⚠️ The first `type-check` attempt returned exit 2 with `TS2307 Cannot find module
'@object-ui/plugin-view'` and siblings — that is a **precondition not met** (an unbuilt
workspace closure), **NOT MEASURED** and not a red gate. It was re-run to exit 0 after
`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/app-shell^..." build`.

## ⚠️ Declared narrowing — the shared verify lock

Two consecutive `os-verify-lock.sh` acquisitions returned `VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99)`,
540s budget each, ~18 minutes queued with zero progress, both behind the same named holder
(pid 17499, a sibling dispatch running the full repo `pnpm test`, held 2253s then 2793s). The
slot was set before the first attempt, so the second resumed the ticket rather than re-queueing.

**Narrowed to** path-filtered vitest runs executed without the lock, `--maxWorkers=2`, under
`--max-old-space-size=4096` — no build, no full `pnpm test`, no turbo fan-out. The later
`build` and `type-check` runs *did* get the lock once it freed and went through it.

**The lit control for the narrowing**: the ablation was run through the same unlocked runner.
A degraded or mis-targeted runner would return the mutated tree green; it returns red on
exactly the predicted rows and green on the predicted others, so the unlocked runner is live
and discriminating.

**Still owed to CI**: full `pnpm test`, `turbo run type-check` across the fan-out, `pnpm lint`.

## Ablation — prediction written before running

Recorded before either mutation. Resolution note: the pin reaches its subject by a **relative**
import (`./flow-node-config`), a sibling module in the same package, **not** through a
dependency's `exports` map — so no `dist/` rebuild sits between mutation and reading, and the
dist-preflight arm does not apply. (`@objectstack/spec` *is* reached through its exports map,
but the spec is never mutated.)

| mutation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** — revert `loop`'s placeholder | 转红, **partial and asymmetric**: the table-reading rows red, every spec-reading row green | **exit 1 — 4 failed / 7 passed.** Red: the descriptor row, the zh-overlay row, the cross-group sweep, the rendered-placeholder row. Green: all 4 spec rows, the alias row, the `defaultValue`-fence row, the stored-value row. **Matches.** |
| **B** — break the fenced-off `map` twin | 转红, **mirrored**: the `map` sweep arm red, the `loop` rows green | **exit 1 — 1 failed / 10 passed.** Red: exactly `the map group hints the identifier its own schema applies`. **Matches.** |

The asymmetry in A is the load-bearing part: it proves the pin measures the **form table** and
could not be satisfied by the schema alone. B proves the `map` lit control is **live** — a
control that stayed green under B would make every negative paired with it a void reading.

Disk proof for each mutation (⛔ never an editor exit code): the subject's blob hash changed
from its `HEAD` blob, plus an anchor grep count on both the injected and the removed text.
Restore proved **by state** on both legs — `git diff HEAD` empty **and** `git hash-object`
matching the `HEAD` blob exactly — with an absolute-path `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` behind it.
Both mutations were applied by re-running the group-boundary sweep and asserting the resolved
row was inside the intended group and outside the other, so neither could stray across the fence.

## A vacuity guard the pin carries

If the installed spec ever stopped defaulting `iteratorVariable`, the derived identifier would
go `undefined` and every equality here would pass by comparing two absences. The pin asserts
the derived identifier is a non-empty string **first**, so that change reddens rather than
hollowing the suite out quietly. The sweep likewise walks **every** node type and fails loudly
on a group that grows the key with no schema mapped — rather than skipping it, which is how a
third instance would hide.

## Out of scope, deliberately

- ⛔ **`map` is untouched.** It agreed already. It is now pinned as a live control.
- ⛔ **`FlowNodeInspector.declaredDefault.test.tsx`** and its false "exactly two boolean fields
  and both declare one" rationale: another card's, and the row it justifies still measures
  something real. **I did not touch that file at all**, so that sentence is exactly as it was.
- `flow-scope.test.ts` uses `currentItem` as a **stored, explicit** iterator value. The probe
  shows that is a legitimate accepted value, so it is correct as written and unchanged.

## Acceptance notes — observed, ⛔ nothing filed

**A bounded sweep for a second instance of this defect class came back clean, and it is lit.**
Every `text` / `number` descriptor in `FLOW_NODE_CONFIG` whose placeholder is a bare
identifier (the "this hint names a variable" shape) was held against the default its own spec
schema applies:

```
node_type       key               form hints     spec applies    verdict
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
loop            iteratorVariable  item           item            AGREE
map             iteratorVariable  item           item            AGREE
map             outputVariable    results        undefined       no default applied -> hint is free
create_record   outputVariable    newRecord      undefined       no default applied -> hint is free
get_record      outputVariable    records        undefined       no default applied -> hint is free
subflow         outputVariable    subResult      undefined       no default applied -> hint is free
http_request    outputVariable    response       (export absent) SKIPPED
notify          topic / sourceObject             (no schema mapped) SKIPPED
legacy_action   outputVariable    result         (no schema mapped) SKIPPED
```

The AGREE rows are what make this a reading rather than an empty sweep. The `undefined` rows
are **not** the same defect: the spec applies no default to those keys, so a blank box binds
nothing and the placeholder is a free example rather than a claim about what the author gets.
Three rows are honest gaps in the sweep (no schema mapped / export absent), not clean readings.
⛔ Nothing filed — no reproducible defect, no contract violated. Successor for these rows:
objectui#9109 fence 4, which is the change that will make hint and default stop being
re-typed by hand.

**The spec's `itemVariable` alias does not make the key acceptable** — `aliases:
{ itemVariable: 'iteratorVariable' }` on `LoopConfigSchema` enriches the refusal message
("Did you mean `itemVariable` -> `iteratorVariable`?") but the key is still refused
(`unrecognized_keys`). That is what the alias is documented to do — it overrules edit distance
in the *suggester* — so it is behaving as designed. ⛔ Not filed. Successor: none.

## Clause-②

**`Clause-②: no`** — re-declared against the diff, not inherited as a prediction.
`flow-node-config.ts` is not exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`; the diff changes
one string literal inside a module-private table plus a comment, adds a test file, and adds a
changeset. No key is added, no accept set moves, no published surface widens. ⇒ no
`needs:contract-review`.
